sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The athach is a monster of Scottish Gaelic folklore. Its name means giant, champion, or monster. It resembles Old Irish aithech, a word for boor or serf. The athach haunted the Scottish Highlands and killed passersby, hurling them into gorges or down rocky hills. Tradition also set it in lonely lochans and lakes. The athach had male and female variants. The female luideag haunted Skye. The male díreach of Glen Etive had one hand growing from his chest and one eye in his forehead. Folklore compares the athach to the bòcan, the díreach, the fachan, and the luideag. The figure connects to the Fachan.

okr.objective: Establish the athach as a Scottish Gaelic monster with male and female variants.
key_results: The athach haunted the Scottish Highlands, gorges, and lonely lochans.
The male díreach of Glen Etive had one hand from the chest and one eye in the forehead.
Folklore compares the athach to the bòcan, díreach, fachan, and luideag.
